newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKET - First Comm enlivens dog days.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKET - First Comm enlivens dog days.

text.p: A pair of new launches on the last Friday of August heralded the end of a slow summer for the Asian debt market.
A US$150 million floating rate certificate of deposit from one of Taiwan's premier banks, First Commercial Bank, was the highlight of Friday's action.
The issuer is about 70 percent owned by the Taiwanese government.
The five-year facility has a call option in year three but no put option.

The certificate was priced at par to float at 20 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate. The A2-rated issuer managed to obtain low cost of funding by controversially paying only a 24 basis point all-in return for top-tier managers.
The arranger group consists of WestLB, Citicorp International, Tokyo Mitsubishi, ANZ International Merchant Bank and Sumitomo Finance.
Bankers said the paper's scarcity value plus the issuer's financial strength underpinned its tight spread and bolstered the tone of the issue.
However, other bankers warned that the "unreasonably aggressive" pricing might heighten investor risk in secondary trade and thus dampen enthusiasm for the deal.
The certificates are only callable in favour of the issuer, a rare feature that clearly distinguishes them from other Asian debt paper.
"Sometimes, you just have to give way to win the bid," a banker noted.
The tightly priced deal sets a benchmark for upcoming transactions from Taiwan.
Bankers commented that Bank of Taiwan, which is 100 percent owned by Taiwanese government, is likely to push for even tighter pricing for its upcoming FRCD issue.

In other news, Jardine Fleming privately placed a HK$75 million floating rate certificate of depsite issue for International Bank of Asia. The one-year issue was priced at par to float at 30 basis points over HIBOR.
Innovative International (HK) Ltd's HK$200 million two- tranche loan facility also went into general syndication via BNP Hong Kong.

Tranche A is a HK$120 million amortising term loan facility and tranche B is a HK$80 million revolver. The three-year facility pays an interest margin of 125 basis points over HIBOR. Fees for top-tier managers are 75 basis points.
Looking ahead, a spate of new issues is to appear in the Asian market in the coming weeks.

Guoco Group's US$180 million floating rate note, Union Bank of Hong Kong's floating rate certificate of deposit and KEB Hong Kong's Hong Kong dollar FRCD are all tentatively scheduled to be launched in early September.
